newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso pares strength, dollar puts exercised.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso pares strength, dollar puts exercised.

text.p: The Mexican peso ceded some ground gained from the dollar in earlier trade by the close on Tuesday, as banks chose to exercise dollar puts previously auctioned by the central bank, traders said.
"Banco de Mexico's dollar puts capped the increase in the peso's strength," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 2.2 and 2.1 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8960/7.8980 and 7.8910/7.8940 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.95 centavos firmer at 7.8760/7.8780 per dollar.

Dealers said the peso had firmed up in early trade on foreign capital inflow into the Mexican secondary money market after yields on U.S. long bonds fell sharply after the release of mild U.S. inflation data.
In late trade, the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was down 29/32 to 7.09 percent.
"There was capital inflow as (U.S.) long bond yields were low and high interest rates we are paying here in Mexico are attractive," another trader said.

Money market dealers surveyed by Reuters said they expected Banco de Mexico to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes rates at an average of 23.16 percent at Tuesday evening's primary auction. This would be a rise of 83 basis points since last week.
Auction results are due to be released at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
"Local dealers were also dumping long dollar positions to pick up paper (CEtes)," a trader said.
